transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hello Doctor. Thank you kindly for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time... is it alright that I'm here? 

My wife, she thought I should come talk to you. It's... well, I don't want you to think poorly of an old man, but... I've been noticing some things. When I'm sitting with the men at the domino table, and... and sometimes even the announcer on the radio, too. They've been giving these little messages. Just meant for me, you see. 

My wife, she says it's just regular talk and I shouldn't pay it no mind, but... well, I know they're warning me to be careful. I hope it's okay that I came to ask you about it... am I explaining that alright?
When you hear the announcer on the radio or when you're with others at the domino table, do you feel like they're actually speaking to you or saying things that aren't really there?

Well, no, not... not exactly saying things that aren't there, I don't think. I mean, the radio announcer is definitely talking on the radio, you know? It just... it feels like the words are pointed right at me. I hope that doesn't sound too foolish. 

But... well, since you're asking about hearing things... I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything, Doctor. It's just a little thing. Sometimes, in the afternoons when the house is real quiet and my wife is resting... I hear my old friend. He passed on a few years back, God rest his soul. But I'll hear him call my name from out on the porch, or... or sometimes he's humming an old choir song we used to sing. It sounds so clear, just like he's standing right there with me. 

It's actually kind of nice, really, not scary at all. I haven't told my wife because I didn't want to upset her, but... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
Have you ever felt that something is true that others don't seem to understand, even when they tell you otherwise?

Well, yes sir... I suppose that's exactly like what I was mentioning when I first sat down. I hope you don't mind me bringing it up again. 

But... with the men at the domino table, and that fellow on the radio? My wife, bless her heart, she tells me otherwise. She says it's just regular talk and I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. And I really hate to disagree with her, Doctor, I don't want you to think I'm being a stubborn or difficult old man. 

But... well, even when she says that, I just know they're giving me those little messages. I know they're warning me to be careful. She just doesn't understand it because the messages aren't meant for her, you see. I hope I'm explaining that right... does that make sense, Doctor?
Doctor: When you feel like people are giving you messages, do you believe this with absolute certainty, even though others don't see it the same way?

Well, yes, Doctor... I suppose I do. I hope that doesn't make me sound too... too set in my ways. I know my wife thinks I'm just being a silly old man, and I really do try to listen to her. She's a good woman, and I don't want to cause any fuss. 

But... when I'm sitting there, or listening to the radio... it's just so clear to me. Even if nobody else catches it, I know in my heart they're warning me to be careful. It's not that I want to argue with anyone about it, no sir. I just... I can't help but know it's true. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from... am I being helpful with these answers?
Doctor: Have these messages or warnings ever felt like part of a larger pattern or plan, like someone is watching you or trying to communicate something important to you over time?

Well... I don't know if I'd call it a big, grand plan, exactly. I don't want you to think I'm making up wild spy stories or anything like that, Doctor. I'd hate for you to think I'm completely losing my marbles. 

It's really just... well, like I was saying before, it's the whole reason I came in to see you. Over time, it just feels like those men at the domino table, and sometimes that announcer on the radio... they keep giving me those little messages meant just for me. And even when my wife says it is just talk—and I really do respect her opinion, I do—I just know they are warning me to be careful. 

I don't think there's anyone hiding in the bushes watching my every move, no sir. It's just... they keep communicating that I need to watch my step. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, bringing it up again. Did I answer your question all right, Doctor?
Do you ever feel like these messages are part of someone trying to harm you or protect you in some way?

Well, I wouldn't say anyone is trying to harm me, Doctor. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I think people are out to get me. I know that would sound awfully strange, and I don't want to be any trouble. 

It's more about... well, protecting me, I suppose. Like I mentioned before, those men at the domino table, and that fellow on the radio... they just slip in those little messages meant for me. Just to warn me to be careful, you know? Like they're looking out for an old man. 

My wife, she thinks I'm just getting confused in my old age, and maybe she's right to worry about me. I hate to worry her. But I just know those warnings are real, even if she says it's just regular talk. I hope it's okay that I feel that way... I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise. Does that make sense to you, Doctor?
Can you tell me more about how you know these messages are meant for you? Have you noticed any specific patterns or reasons why you think these people are choosing to warn you?

Well... I hope you don't think I'm being silly, Doctor. I really don't want to take up too much of your time with an old man's foolishness. But... well, it's just the way they look at me, I suppose. The men at the domino table, I mean. They'll be talking about the weather or the news, and then... they'll use a certain word, or give me a little nod. 

It's the same with the radio. The announcer will be talking, and then... it's like he pauses just a second, just for me. Like a little signal. I know my wife thinks I'm making a mountain out of a molehill, and I really do try to see it her way. I don't want to be a bother to her, or to you. 

But I just know they're warning me to be careful. I don't know why they picked me, exactly... maybe they just see an old fellow and think I need looking after. I'm sorry if that sounds a bit ridiculous. I hope I'm explaining it right... is that what you were asking, Doctor?

Are these messages the only unusual experiences you've been having, or have you noticed other things that others might not understand, like thoughts being placed in your mind or objects having special hidden meanings?

Well, no, nobody's putting thoughts in my head, nothing like that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely losing my grip on reality, Doctor. And I don't see secret meanings in objects around the house or anything strange like that. 

But... well, I suppose there is one other little thing. I hesitate to even mention it, because I know how it sounds, and I'd hate for you to think I'm making up stories. It's really nothing bad, though. Just... sometimes, in the afternoons, when my wife is resting and the house is real quiet... 

I hear my old friend, from years back. I'll hear him call my name from out on the porch, plain as day. Or sometimes he'll be humming one of the old choir songs we used to sing. It sounds so clear, Doctor, just like he's standing right there next to me. 

I know it sounds a bit odd, and I don't usually tell people because I don't want to be a nuisance or have anyone worry. It's rather comforting, honestly, just a friendly voice. I hope you don't think less of me for mentioning it... is it okay that I told you about that?
Have you ever felt that these messages are part of a bigger plot or that there's a hidden group or organization involved in sending them to you?

Oh, my, no... no, nothing like that, Doctor. I really hope I haven't made you think I believe in... well, secret organizations or spy plots or anything grand like that. I know that would sound terribly crazy, and I certainly don't want you to think I've lost my mind entirely. I'd hate to give you that impression.

Like I was trying to say earlier—and I am so sorry if I didn't explain it right the first time—that's really the whole reason I came in to see you. It's just those regular fellows at the domino table, and sometimes that one radio announcer. Just them giving me those little messages meant for me. 

There's no big hidden group behind it. It's just... well, even when my wife tells me it is just everyday talk, I just know they are warning me to be careful. Just looking out for me, in their own way. I hope it doesn't make me sound too stubborn or difficult, going against what my wife says... I really do try to be agreeable with her. Did I answer your question alright, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
